prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2010 manifesto pledges a “future fair for all” built on three pillars: rebuilding a balanced, high-tech economy; protecting and reforming frontline public services; and renewing politics to restore trust.

Economy and public finances
- Secure the recovery (no 2010 cuts), then more than halve the deficit in four years via growth, fair tax rises (50p top rate, NI +1p, banker bonus tax, reduced pension relief for the best off), £20bn+ efficiency savings, a pay cap, pension reform and asset sales.
- Tough banking reform: higher capital, “living wills,” bonus restraint, a global levy, stronger FSA powers, greater competition and possible mutualisation options for Northern Rock.
- Active industrial strategy: UK Finance for Growth (£4bn), R&D credits, patent box, higher capital allowances, a Green Investment Bank, high-speed rail, superfast broadband for all, energy and digital infrastructure. Promote long-termism with a two‑thirds shareholder threshold for takeovers.
- Support SMEs and entrepreneurs: rates holiday, credit adjudicator, extended Time to Pay, doubled Entrepreneurs’ Relief, less red tape.

Jobs, welfare and living standards
- Job guarantees: 200,000 places via the Future Jobs Fund; mandatory work after two years’ unemployment; tighter incapacity reassessments; Better Off in Work guarantee (+£40/week).
- Minimum wage to rise at least with average earnings; expand apprenticeships and Skills Accounts.
- Housing: stamp duty holiday for first‑time buyers up to £250k (funded by 5% rate over £1m), more affordable and council homes, tougher mortgage regulation, private landlord register, aim to end rough sleeping by 2012.
- Consumer finance: People’s Bank at the Post Office; universal right to a basic bank account; clampdown on high‑cost lenders; single consumer credit regulator; portable account/ISA numbers.

Education
- Protect/increase frontline spending on Sure Start, childcare, schools and 16–19 learning; expand free nursery places for 2–4s.
- Guarantees: catch‑up tuition in the 3Rs; personal tutors; broader curriculum; stronger discipline; parental “trigger” to change failing leadership; growth of accredited school groups, academies and co‑ops.
- Raise participation to 18; expand advanced apprenticeships and HE (ring‑fenced science).

Health and care
- Protect NHS budget; reinvest up to £20bn efficiencies; legally backed guarantees (18‑week treatment or go private; 1‑week cancer test results); choose any qualified provider; evening/weekend GP access; more prevention and mental health therapy.
- National Care Service: free home care for highest needs (from 2011), a cap on residential costs after two years (from 2014), and a path to comprehensive, free-at-point-of-use adult care post‑2015.

Families and older people
- “Fathers’ Month” paid leave; more flexible working (including for older workers); end default retirement at 65; restore earnings link for the Basic State Pension (from 2012); Personal Pension Accounts.

Security, borders and justice
- Maintain police/PCSO numbers; neighbourhood policing; action on failing forces; faster, tougher responses to ASB; expand Community Payback; proportionate use of CCTV/DNA.
- Points‑based immigration system; tougher English requirements; curb abuse; benefits increasingly reserved for citizens/permanent residents.

Culture, environment and places
- Olympics legacy; stronger school sport; supporter ownership in football; museums’ operational independence; protect post offices and pubs; uphold BBC independence.
- Green transition: about 40% low‑carbon electricity by 2020 (renewables, nuclear, CCS); 400,000 green jobs by 2015; home insulation (“pay as you save”), smart meters, zero‑waste drive; protect Green Belt, expand forests; rural broadband and services; Supermarket Ombudsman.

Political reform and global role
- Referendums on AV and an elected second chamber; fixed‑term parliaments; lobbyist register; recall for misconduct; stronger devolution; open data and digital government.
- Afghanistan strategy with troop support; Strategic Defence Review; maintain independent nuclear deterrent; lead in the EU; enshrine 0.7% aid by 2013; drive MDGs, human rights and reform of global institutions.
